summary: The root Q-T-L, beyond its common meaning of "to kill," can also mean "to know something thoroughly." It implies a deep, complete understanding, as if one has mastered the knowledge of that thing.
lane: 1 قَتَلَ الشَّىْءَ ذ , inf. n. قَتْلٌ , (assumed tropical:) He knew the thing; he was, or became, acquainted with it: (Msb:) [or rather, i. q. ] قَتَلَهُ عِلْمًا , (Bd in iv. 156, and TA,) and خُبْرًا , (K,) and بِعِلْمِهِ , (Bd, ubi supra,) he knew it (Bd, K, TA) completely, (TA,) or thoroughly, very well, or superlatively well; as also نَحَرَهُ عِلْمًا . (Bd.) See أَثْبَتَ الشَّىْء مَعْرِفَةً in art. ثبت .

headwords.def: قَتَلَ الشَّىْءَ , inf. n. قَتْلٌ, (assumed tropical:) He knew the thing; he was, or became, acquainted with it: (Msb:) [or rather, i. q. ] قَتَلَهُ عِلْمًا, (Bd in iv. 156, and TA,) and خُبْرًا, (K,) and بِعِلْمِهِ, (Bd, ubi supra,) he knew it (Bd, K, TA) completely, (TA,) or thoroughly, very well, or superlatively well; as also نَحَرَهُ عِلْمًا. (Bd.) See أَثْبَتَ الشَّىْء مَعْرِفَةً in art. ثبت.
: see a verse cited in art. عتب, conj. 4.
He fought, or combated, him; contended with him in fight or conflict or battle. قَاتَلَ عَلَى دِيِن ٱللّٰهِ: see 3 in art. ازى.
تَقَتَّلَتْ لَهُ means تَخَضَّعَتْ لَهُ وَتَ َلَّلَتْ حَتَّى عَشِقَهَا. (A.)

[properly He sought, or courted, slaughter; ] i. q. اِسْتَمَاتَ; (S, K;) meaning he cared not for death, by reason of his courage; (JM;) he resigned and subjected himself to slaughter, and cared not for death. (Mgh.)
: from this word is formed the pl. قُتُولٌ, on the authority of hearsay. (El-Jurjánee, in Msb, art. قصد.)
[ Murderous; slaughterous; very deadly. ] You say حَيَّةٌ قَتَّالَهٌ [ A very deadly serpent ]. (TA in art. اصل.)
Deadly; applied to a tree; (K in art. خمط;) and to poison. (TA in that art.)
A [ vital ] place in a man [or an animal, i. e.] where a wound causes death; (S, Msb;) as the temple: (Msb:) pl. مَقَاتِلُ. (S.)
وَلِنِّى مَقَاتِلَكَ means حَوِّلْ إِلَىَّ وَجْهَكَ. (A.)

headword_note: Lane organises by verb form and principal noun, not by every inflected form. A word with no headword entry falls back to the root meaning; nothing is inferred.
mentions_note: Forms Lane discusses inside another entry rather than defining as a headword. Values index into headwords[].
